sample_unit: patient information leaflets (7 LLM-generated, 1 Stroke Association)

links.outcome: Reading level of patient leaflets (FKG, FRE, ARI, GFI)
links.effect: Median Flesch-Kincaid grade 8.5 (secondary-school band) across all leaflets; AI-generated texts generally clearer than the Stroke Association leaflet.
links.quote: Across all leaflets, readability remained within a secondary-school band (median FKG 8.5), with AI-generated texts generally clearer but less well-referenced.

links.outcome: Referencing quality of LLM-generated leaflets (0-2 scale)
links.effect: Stroke Association leaflet had perfect referencing; AI-generated texts were less well-referenced.
links.quote: The Stroke Association leaflet achieved perfect factual accuracy and referencing, whereas Microsoft Copilot and DeepSeek demonstrated occasional omissions in seizure and transient ischemic attack (TIA) guidance.

links.outcome: Factual accuracy/misinformation of leaflet content on driving after stroke
links.effect: Stroke Association leaflet had perfect factual accuracy; Copilot and DeepSeek showed occasional omissions in seizure and TIA guidance.
links.quote: The Stroke Association leaflet achieved perfect factual accuracy and referencing, whereas Microsoft Copilot and DeepSeek demonstrated occasional omissions in seizure and transient ischemic attack (TIA) guidance.

screen.reason: Evaluates readability, reliability, and accuracy of LLM-generated patient leaflets on driving after stroke compared to a professional gold standard.
